name: ElevenLabs
look: Off-white canvas with warm near-black ink, no saturated CTA colour, and pastel gradient orbs carrying all the brand voltage.

hero.title: The most realistic voice AI platform
hero.sub: Text to speech in thirty-two languages, voice cloning from sixty seconds of audio, and dubbing that keeps the performance rather than flattening it.

features.title: Voice that carries the performance
features.sub: Prosody, emphasis and breath — the parts that make synthesis stop sounding synthetic.

items.title: Text to speech
items.body: Thirty-two languages with emotion and pacing inferred from the text rather than dictated by tags.

items.title: Voice cloning
items.body: A usable clone from sixty seconds of clean audio, with consent verification built into the flow.

items.title: Dubbing
items.body: Translate and re-voice a video while keeping the original speaker's timbre and timing.

items.title: Streaming
items.body: Seventy-five millisecond first-byte latency, fast enough for a live conversational agent.

items.title: Fine control
items.body: Stability, similarity and style exposed as dials, with the defaults tuned for narration.

items.title: Provenance
items.body: Every generation is watermarked and traceable, and cloning requires verified consent.

showcases.title: The same performance, another language
showcases.body: Dubbing preserves the speaker's timbre and the timing of the original delivery, so a translated documentary still sounds like the person who made it rather than a stock narrator reading a transcript.
points: Timing matched to the original delivery

showcases.title: Consent and provenance, by design
showcases.body: Voice cloning requires verified consent from the speaker, every generation carries an inaudible watermark, and there is a public tool for checking whether a clip came from us.

gallery.title: Voice library
gallery.sub: Thousands of voices shared by their owners, each with the licence terms attached.

testimonial.quote: We dubbed a forty-minute documentary into six languages in an afternoon. The director's note was that the Portuguese version sounded more like him than the English one did.
testimonial.name: Léa Moreau

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Free to start. Characters roll over on paid plans.

items.a: No. Cloning requires verified consent from the speaker, captured through a recorded confirmation phrase. Uploading someone else's audio without it will not produce a clone.

items.q: Who owns the audio I generate?
items.a: You do, on any paid plan, including commercial use. Free-tier output is licensed for non-commercial use and must credit the platform.
Every generation carries an inaudible signal that survives normal compression. A public tool checks whether a clip originated here, and it is free to use.
Seventy-five milliseconds to first byte on the streaming endpoint, measured from the nearest region. Full-file generation is slower and depends on length.

cta.title: Hear it for yourself
cta.sub: Ten thousand characters free, no card, and the voice library is open from the start.

footer.tagline: Voice AI that carries the performance.

notes: There is no saturated CTA colour. The single primary action is an ink pill, and all the brand voltage comes from the atmospheric gradients.
Pastel gradient orbs — mint, peach, lavender, sky, rose — are decoration only. Putting one behind a button breaks the system.
Display runs at weight 300 for an editorial magazine voice; body is a sans at 400 with slightly positive tracking.
Geometry is soft: pills for CTAs, generous rounding on cards, nothing sharp.
Section rhythm is 96px throughout, which is what keeps the page feeling unhurried.
